questions.explanation: ATP stands for adenosine triphosphate. It is a molecule consisting of adenine, ribose sugar, and three phosphate groups that serves as the energy currency of cells.

questions.stem: Why is ATP called the energy currency of the cell?

options.text: Because it is stored in banks
Because it is made of gold
Because it is used to transfer energy to power cellular processes, just as currency is used to pay for things

questions.explanation: ATP is called the energy currency because it provides immediate, usable energy for cellular processes. Energy from respiration is stored in ATP and released when cells need it.

questions.stem: How is energy released from ATP?

options.text: By hydrolysis - removing the third phosphate group, converting ATP to ADP and releasing energy

questions.explanation: Energy is released when the bond between the second and third phosphate groups is broken by hydrolysis. ATP is converted to ADP (adenosine diphosphate) and an inorganic phosphate.

questions.stem: What is the relationship between respiration and ATP?

options.text: ATP is broken down during respiration
Respiration produces ATP by transferring energy from glucose to form ATP from ADP and phosphate

questions.explanation: Respiration transfers the chemical energy in glucose to produce ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. This ATP then provides energy for all cellular activities.

options.text: Active transport, muscle contraction, protein synthesis, cell division, nerve impulse transmission

questions.explanation: ATP is used for many processes including active transport across membranes, muscle contraction, synthesising proteins and other molecules, cell division (mitosis), and transmitting nerve impulses.

questions.stem: What is the advantage of using ATP rather than glucose directly for energy?

options.text: ATP releases energy in small, manageable amounts suitable for individual reactions

questions.explanation: ATP releases energy in small, controlled amounts ideal for powering individual cellular reactions. Releasing all the energy from glucose at once would generate too much heat and waste energy.

options.text: Yes, ADP and phosphate are recombined to form ATP again using energy from respiration
No, once used it is destroyed

questions.explanation: ATP is continuously recycled. When ATP is hydrolysed to ADP and phosphate, the energy is used for cell work. ADP is then re-phosphorylated using energy from respiration to regenerate ATP.
